Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 30-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE, MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Reinforcement Learning [NPT_4126]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Discuss the exploration-exploitation tradeoff in RL? Give a short example.                           (2)  
  
  
  A)                                                      Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)           Describe the multi-armed bandit problem and explain how it represents the exploration-exploitation   (3)  
  dilemma.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)           Interpret how the Policy Gradient Theorem helps in directly optimizing stochastic policies. Use an   (5)  
  example of a simple environment (e.g., two-action system) to show how gradients are estimated  
  and used to update the policy parameters. Discuss the advantages of this approach compared to  
  value-based methods.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Discuss the PAC (Probably Approximately Correct) framework in the context of reinforcement           (2)  
  learning.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  B)           Interpret the Policy Gradient Theorem and discuss how it helps in optimizing policy directly.        (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           Compare PAC-based evaluation with regret-based evaluation methods in reinforcement learning.         (5)  
  Highlight key differences in their goals and interpretations.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                Distinguish between value-based and policy-based reinforcement learning methods.                     (2)  
  
  
  A)                                                          Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           Analyze how the Bellman Optimality Principle helps in determining the optimal policy in              (3)  
  reinforcement learning problems.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)           For an autonomous delivery robot navigating between three locations, define an appropriate           (5)  
  
  Page #1

Markov Decision Process (MDP) including states, actions, transition probabilities, and rewards.  
  Using this setup, apply the Bellman equation for the state-value function to compute one iteration of  
  value updates for each state.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)                       Apply the SARSA and Q-learning algorithms on a simple grid-world problem and illustrate how the          (3)  
  Q-values are updated after one episode.  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)               Demonstrate with an example how n-step returns differ from 1-step Temporal Difference (TD)               (3)  
  learning.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)               Interpret the performance of Deep Q-Networks (DQN) compared to traditional Q-learning, citing the (4)  
  role of experience replay and target networks.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5)                       Interpret how the Options Framework in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) helps an agent (3)  
  solve a multi-step task such as "navigating a maze with sub-goals."  
  A)  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)               Examine the role of temporal abstraction in Hierarchical RL, and how it improves learning efficiency (3)  
  in complex tasks.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)               Given a scenario of a self-driving car operating under uncertain sensor inputs, apply the POMDP          (4)  
  framework to model the problem. Describe possible solution methods for policy optimization under  
  partial observability.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  
  -----End-----
